teaching_language: ENGLISH — 100% English-taught, and this is not merely a marketing claim but a legally binding clause of the programme's Didactic Regulations, because the English requirement is justified precisely by the delivery language. DIRECT EVIDENCE: (1) the official orientation portal fact-sheet header records "Language ENG" (a single value; other Federico II courses in the same catalogue show "IT/ENG"); (2) the Didactic Regulations of the Degree Program (Art. 4, c. 1) state "...have at least a B2 level of English that will be evaluated through a special pre-registration interview. This requirement is mandatory for the admission, since all the courses will be entirely taught in English."; (3) Art. 5, c. 3 repeats "Since this is a Degree Course whose teaching activities will be delivered entirely in English, this requirement is mandatory for admission."; (4) the central unina.it record states the same in its "Conoscenze richieste per l'accesso" section; (5) the entire official 2026/2027 Study Plan is published with every course title in English; (6) the thesis must be written in English — "the passing of the final test which involves the discussion of a written thesis, drafted in English in an original way by the student". A dedicated 6-CFU first-year course "Academic English" (SSD 10/ANGL-01) is built into the common route, and the Didactic Regulations add "Further refinement of English with advanced instruction aimed at using the language in an international relations context is possibly planned." ITALIAN IS NOT REQUIRED — neither at admission nor, on the evidence available on unina.it, to graduate: unlike some other Federico II English-taught degrees (e.g. Data Science), NO unina.it page for International Relations attaches an Italian-language CLA certificate to the "other training activities" (TAF F) credits. The 6-CFU TAF F slot is described neutrally as "additional language skills, seminars, workshops, observatories, internships, and other activities designed to support entry into the labour market". THE ONE REAL LANGUAGE COMPLICATION IS A THIRD LANGUAGE, NOT ITALIAN [uncertain]: both the Didactic Regulations and the central unina.it record state that "the study of an additional non-EU language (Chinese or Arabic) is planned during the course", and the orientation portal says "in their second year (once, again, for both curricula), students can choose between two foreign languages (Arabic or Chinese)". HOWEVER, the binding a.y. 2026/2027 Study Plan PDF contains NO Arabic or Chinese course in either curriculum — the only language course listed anywhere is the first-year Academic English. Either the Arabic/Chinese requirement has been quietly absorbed into the free-choice (D) or additional (F) slots, or it has been dropped and the Regulations/SUA text is stale. Applicants counting on learning Arabic or Chinese inside the degree should confirm with the coordinator before enrolling. SECOND, SMALLER CAVEAT: the elective (TAF D) slot allows students to "freely choose from among the courses offered by the University" — courses taken from Italian-taught degrees would obviously be delivered in Italian, but the three electives the Department itself recommends (International food and agricultural policy, International marketing, Global environmental politics) are all listed under English titles in the English Study Plan.

admission_type: NOT NUMERUS CLAUSUS AND NOT PLAIN OPEN ACCESS — the official classification on the orientation portal fact-sheet is "Admission: Verifica di preparazione" (verification of preparation), i.e. access is unlimited in number but conditional on passing a COMPULSORY, individually-scheduled ENGLISH-LANGUAGE INTERVIEW plus a curricular-credit check. There is no ranking list, no score-based competition and no seat cap; every candidate who meets the curricular requirements and passes the interview can enrol. Federico II reserves the label "Libero" (free) for degrees with no gate at all, and this programme is deliberately NOT labelled that way. THE PROCEDURE HAS THREE COMPONENTS. (1) CURRICULAR REQUIREMENT CHECK — automatic for holders of an Italian L-16 or L-36 bachelor; a documentary evaluation of the transcript for everyone else (see academic_requirements). (2) COMPULSORY VERIFICATION OF PERSONAL PREPARATION — Didactic Regulations Art. 5, c. 2: "Verification of personal preparation is always mandatory, and only students who meet the curricular requirements can access it." Note the ordering: you must clear the credit gate BEFORE you are allowed to sit the verification. (3) COMPULSORY ENGLISH INTERVIEW — a "special pre-enrolment interview" (colloquio di verifica della conoscenza della lingua inglese) held on fixed dates announced by the Department (see entry_exam_or_test). ROUTE FOR ITALIAN / EU APPLICANTS: register for the interview by e-mail to the Orientation Desk, sit the interview, then matriculate through the ordinary University enrolment procedure at the Segreteria Studenti Area didattica Scienze Politiche. Italian applicants whose bachelor is not L-16/L-36 are told to get their transcript pre-checked: "Italian students interested in enrolling in the MA in International Relations are required to meet specific credit requirements in certain subject areas. For personalised guidance on whether your undergraduate degree meets these requirements, please contact Dr. Erminia Morone at erminia.morone@unina.it before submitting your application." ROUTE FOR NON-EU APPLICANTS RESIDING ABROAD: compulsory pre-enrolment on the ministerial UNIVERSITALY portal naming Federico II and this programme, with a pre-acceptance letter from the Programme Coordinator, then a study visa, then matriculation in Naples. NON-EU APPLICANTS ALREADY LEGALLY RESIDENT IN ITALY OR THE EU are treated like EU applicants and do NOT pre-enrol on Universitaly. academic_requirements: A THREE-YEAR ITALIAN BACHELOR IN CLASS L-16 OR L-36 (or an equivalent qualification under earlier Italian regulations) GIVES DIRECT ACCESS; everything else goes through a credit count. VERBATIM RULE (Didactic Regulations, Art. 4): "Eligible students for the Master's Degree Program in International Relations are only those who hold a three-year degree in the classes L-16, L-36 or equivalent, according to the previous Rules and Regulations, and have at least a B2 level of English that will be evaluated through a special pre-registration interview." (L-16 = Scienze dell'amministrazione e dell'organizzazione / Sciences of Administration and Organisation; L-36 = Scienze politiche e delle relazioni internazionali / Political Science and International Relations.) FOR ALL OTHER BACHELOR CLASSES, Art. 4 cc. 2-3 and Art. 5 c. 3 set a hard, numeric credit threshold: "first-cycle graduates from different degree classes could be admitted and enrolled in the Master's Degree Program in International Relations, but the admission will be subject to a preliminary assessment of the students' curriculum. In this respect, the acquisition of at least 48 ECTS in the basic/foundation and characterizing activities of all the disciplinary fields and related disciplinary sectors, as provided by the ministerial table of the L 36 class, and 12 ECTS in the related or supplementary training activities, according to the Academic Rules and Regulations included in the SUA-CDS of the study courses belonging to the Department of Political Sciences, is a mandatory requirement for admission." SO THE NUMBERS ARE: 48 CFU/ECTS minimum in the base + characterizing SSDs of the ministerial L-36 table, PLUS 12 CFU in related/supplementary activities — 60 CFU of relevant coursework in total. The 48 CFU must sit in the disciplinary sectors that the L-36 ministerial table recognises (political science, history, law, economics, statistics, sociology and cognate SSDs); the interpretation of a foreign transcript against that table is done by the Department, which is why non-standard applicants are told to get pre-checked. ENGLISH B2 IS A SEPARATE, NON-WAIVABLE ADMISSION CONDITION on top of the academic requirement — see language_requirements. PERSONAL PREPARATION: Art. 5, c. 4 — "The student's personal preparation is verified by evaluating his or her previous university career. A student is considered to possess adequate personal preparation, and may therefore enroll in this master's degree program, if he or she meets the curricular requirements set forth in paragraph A and has passed appropriate verification." MISSING CREDITS: the Regulations contain no OFA (additional training obligation) mechanism for this master's, so an applicant short of the 48+12 CFU cannot be admitted "with debts" — the missing credits must be acquired first, which under Federico II rules is done by enrolling in single course units (corsi singoli; the Department publishes a "Domanda di iscrizione a corsi singoli" form, and the University charges 180 EUR for single-course enrolment). CREDIT RECOGNITION ONCE ENROLLED: "Any recognition of CFU relating to examinations passed as single courses may take place within the limit of 36 CFU, upon request of the interested party and following the approval of the CCD", and up to 12 CFU may be recognised for extra-curricular activities. NO INTERNAL PREREQUISITE CHAIN is imposed between courses beyond what Art. 11 provides. LATE-ENROLMENT CFU CONDITION (University-wide): under the 'Guida all'iscrizione a.a. 2026-27', students enrolling in a two-year master's after 31 December 2026 may be required by the course's Teaching Coordination Commission (CCD) to first acquire between 6 and 12 CFU through single course units. [uncertain] TWO GAPS: (a) no unina.it page publishes the list of foreign bachelor degrees deemed "equivalent" to L-16/L-36, nor a conversion rule for foreign transcripts, so a non-Italian applicant cannot self-assess the 48+12 CFU test from unina.it alone — the Department's answer is to write to erminia.morone@unina.it; (b) unlike some Federico II master's degrees, NO minimum bachelor GRADE (GPA) threshold is published anywhere on unina.it for this programme.

seats_total: NO SEAT CAP PUBLISHED — the programme is not a "corso a numero programmato". Its official admission classification is "Verifica di preparazione", which under Federico II's taxonomy means an entry check without a numerical limit, as opposed to "Programmato" (capped). Three corroborating facts: (1) no unina.it page for International Relations LM-52 / LM-52e states a number of places, a ranking, or a cut-off; (2) the University's central index of admission calls for capped courses (https://www.unina.it/didattica/offerta-didattica/corsi-a-numero-programmato/bandi-di-ammissione, tabs Triennali / Magistrali / Magistrali a ciclo unico) does not list International Relations — as of 2026-08-30 that page returned "Al momento non sono pervenuti nuovi contenuti" (no content currently available) for the current cycle; (3) the Didactic Regulations, Art. 5 c. 1, treat any capping as an exception imposed from outside — "The CCD of the Degree Program normally regulates the admission criteria and any scheduling of enrolments, except in the case subject to different provisions of law", with a footnote pointing to L. 264/1999 (the national numerus clausus law) which does not cover LM-52. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: there is no competitive cut-off to beat and no risk of being ranked out; the only gates are the 48+12 CFU curricular check and the English interview. language_requirements: ENGLISH AT CEFR B2 OR ABOVE — a mandatory, non-waivable admission condition, VERIFIED BY A LIVE INTERVIEW rather than purely on paper. This is the distinguishing feature of this programme's admission: where most Federico II English-taught degrees accept a certificate as sufficient proof, LM-52e requires candidates to sit a compulsory oral verification. THE BINDING WORDINGS: central unina.it record, "Accesso al Corso: Laurea di 1° livello e conoscenza della lingua inglese almeno di livello B2"; Didactic Regulations Art. 4, "...have at least a B2 level of English that will be evaluated through a special pre-registration interview. This requirement is mandatory for the admission, since all the courses will be entirely taught in English."; Didactic Regulations Art. 5 c. 3, "...possess a certified knowledge of English at least level B2, which will be assessed through a special pre-registration interview."; Department page, "English language at least of level B2 which will be evaluated through a special pre-enrolment interview. Being a Degree Course, whose teaching activities will be delivered entirely in English, this requirement is mandatory for access."; orientation portal, "Knowledge of the English language should be officially certified and will be tested through a colloquium at the beginning of the degree." [uncertain] NOTE THE TENSION BETWEEN "CERTIFIED" AND "INTERVIEWED": Art. 4 requires only that the B2 level "will be evaluated through" the interview (no certificate mentioned), while Art. 5 and the orientation portal say the knowledge should be "certified". Read together, the safest reading is that BOTH are expected — bring an official B2+ certificate AND sit the interview. NO unina.it page publishes a list of accepted certificates, a list of exempting nationalities/degrees, a minimum IELTS/TOEFL score, or a rule waiving the interview for holders of an English-medium bachelor. The University's general admission regulation refers only generically to "an international certificate attesting to the level of English language skills (IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge, etc.)" and notes it "is useful for the issue of the visa by the diplomatic/consular Representation". Confirm your specific certificate with scienzepolitiche.orienta@unina.it or erminia.morone@unina.it before booking travel. HOW AND WHEN THE INTERVIEW IS TAKEN: see entry_exam_or_test (a.y. 2026/2027 first session 16 September 2026, 14:30; register 1-14 September 2026 by e-mail). ITALIAN: NOT REQUIRED, at admission or for the visa. The University-wide rule applies: "If you choose a three-year, five-year or single-cycle degree course in ENGLISH, level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required." And, unlike Federico II's Data Science LM, NO unina.it page for International Relations makes an Italian-language CLA certificate a graduation condition. Italian courses remain available on a voluntary basis through the University Language Centre (CLA, https://www.cla.unina.it/en/home). THIRD LANGUAGE [uncertain]: the Didactic Regulations and the central record state that "the study of an additional non-EU language (Chinese or Arabic) is planned during the course" and the orientation portal says second-year students "can choose between two foreign languages (Arabic or Chinese)" — but no Arabic or Chinese course appears in the binding a.y. 2026/2027 Study Plan. Treat the third language as an optional/elective possibility to be confirmed, not a guaranteed offering. OUTPUT-LANGUAGE RULE: the final thesis must be "drafted in English in an original way by the student" and is defended in an oral discussion. In-programme English support: the compulsory 6-CFU first-year course "Academic English" (Prof. Cristina Pennarola), plus "Further refinement of English with advanced instruction aimed at using the language in an international relations context is possibly planned."
application_deadline_eu: [uncertain] THERE IS NO SINGLE PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC APPLICATION DEADLINE PUBLISHED ON UNINA.IT FOR EU (AND EU-EQUIVALENT) CANDIDATES — instead there are THREE overlapping date sets, and the programme's own consolidated application calendar for international candidates is published off unina.it (see uncertainty_notes). (A) THE OPERATIVE PROGRAMME-LEVEL DEADLINE FOR A.Y. 2026/2027 IS THE ENGLISH-INTERVIEW REGISTRATION WINDOW: 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-14, with the interview itself on 2026-09-16 at 14:30 — "Le iscrizioni per il colloquio ... dovranno essere effettuate dal 1° settembre al 14 settembre 2026", by e-mail to scienzepolitiche.orienta@unina.it. Because the interview is compulsory and precedes enrolment, missing this window means waiting for the (not yet published) second session. In earlier years the Department ran later sittings — 29 November 2023 for a.y. 2023/24, 18 December 2024 for a.y. 2024/25, 21 May 2026 for a.y. 2025/26 (registration by 20 May 2026) — so a second 2026/27 date is likely but is not yet on unina.it. (B) QUALIFICATION EVALUATION FOR EU APPLICANTS WITH A FOREIGN DEGREE — no fixed date: "you have to send your academic documents to the Coordinator of the course you wish to enrol in to find out whether you meet the enrolment requirements" (international.unina.it). Italian applicants outside L-16/L-36 are told to contact Dr. Erminia Morone "before submitting your application". Do this as early as possible — it precedes both the interview and enrolment. (C) UNIVERSITY ENROLMENT (MATRICULATION) CALENDAR FOR A.Y. 2026/2027, from the binding 'Guida all'iscrizione Anno accademico 2026-27', which governs Italian and EU students alike: 2026-07-16 ordinary immatriculation period opens ("16 LUGLIO 2026 - Inizio periodo ordinario immatricolazione"; the instalment table specifies "Dal 16 luglio (immatricolazioni L o iscrizioni I anno LM)", i.e. first-year master's enrolments open on this date); 2026-09-01 ordinary period opens for transfers and course changes; 2026-11-02 ORDINARY DEADLINE for immatriculation and for enrolment in later years, and the deadline for the ISEEU income data to be drawn from the INPS database; 2026-11-03 extraordinary (late) period opens; 2027-01-15 last date to enrol late with a 50 EUR surcharge; 2027-01-16 the late surcharge rises to 110 EUR; 2027-03-31 ABSOLUTE FINAL DEADLINE for first-year enrolment in a two-year master's — "Le iscrizioni al primo anno dei corsi di laurea magistrali potranno essere effettuate entro il 31 marzo 2027", with the condition that anyone enrolling after 2026-12-31 may be required by the CCD to first earn between 6 and 12 CFU via single course units. INSTALMENT DATES: 1st by 2026-11-02, 2nd by 2027-03-01, 3rd by 2027-04-30; a further 100 EUR surcharge applies from 2027-07-16 for unpaid 2nd/3rd instalments. TEACHING START: 21 September 2026 ("INIZIO LEZIONI 21 SETTEMBRE 2026 SEMESTRE I") — note this is BEFORE the 16 September interview result would normally be turned into an enrolment, so plan to be reachable in the second half of September. CONFLICTING UNINA.IT STATEMENT: the orientation portal's "Application timeline" block still says "Bar exceptions connected to the current pandemic; matriculation procedures normally take place between September 1st to October 31st of each academic year" — a stale, pandemic-era sentence whose window (1 Sept - 31 Oct) contradicts the 2026/27 Guida (16 July - 2 Nov, extendable to 31 March 2027). Use the Guida. PRACTICAL ADVICE: register for the September interview in the 1-14 September window, and complete enrolment between the interview and 2 November 2026; treat 31 March 2027 as an emergency fallback that costs you a semester and may cost you 6-12 CFU of single courses.

After this date students who are not officially enrolled according to ministerial regulations will have their visa revoked, and Italian police authorities will be notified." (The same booklet's Matriculation page mistypes this as "31 January 2026"; the Deadlines page and the ministerial rule both give 31 January 2027.) SEQUENCING ADVICE FROM THE UNIVERSITY: "It is advisable to obtain the admission to your chosen programme before applying on Universitaly. Otherwise, if you have already submitted your pre-enrolment application on Universitaly, a dedicated team will forward your documents for evaluation. In this case, processing times may be longer." So secure the Coordinator's pre-acceptance letter well before 15 June. ONE-SHOT WARNING: "I have cancelled my Universitaly application to the University of Naples Federico II. Can I apply again to the same University? No, you cannot. If you cancel your application on Universitaly, you cannot reapply to the same University for the same academic year." Programme changes inside a live application are allowed only within the pre-enrolment deadline. NON-EU APPLICANTS ALREADY LEGALLY RESIDENT IN ITALY OR THE EU are treated like EU applicants — they "have unrestricted access to university courses", do not pre-enrol on Universitaly, and follow the calendar in application_deadline_eu. WHY THIS FIELD IS UNCERTAIN: the orientation portal states that for international students "applications are examined on a rolling basis and results should be made known according to the calendar provided within the call for the admission" and links that call to https://www.international-relations.net/admission — an external domain that this research task's source restriction forbade opening. So the programme's own rolling-review dates, any earlier internal application cut-off, and how the compulsory English interview is scheduled for overseas candidates are NOT verified here. Non-EU applicants should treat 15 June 2026 (for 2027/28: the equivalent June date) as the hard ministerial ceiling and contact scienzepolitiche.orienta@unina.it / pietro.maffettone@unina.it for the programme-side calendar. NOTE ON TIMING AS AT 2026-08-30: the 15 June 2026 non-EU pre-enrolment deadline for a.y. 2026/2027 HAS ALREADY PASSED, so a non-EU reader must target a.y. 2027/2028 and re-check the corresponding booklet when it is published.
required_documents: [uncertain] NO PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC DOCUMENT CHECKLIST IS PUBLISHED ON UNINA.IT. The Department's page carries an "| Admission" menu with the entries "Applications / Call for Admission" and "Administrative Documents / Enrollment Forms / Recognition Of Academic Title - Request Form", but on inspection "Call for Admission" and "Recognition Of Academic Title - Request Form" are rendered as underlined text with NO hyperlink at all, and "Enrollment Forms" points to a text-fragment anchor ("#:~:text=Admin%20Forms%20English%20Version") to a section that does not exist in the served page. The list below is therefore assembled from University-level sources plus the departmental forms library. (1) TO REGISTER FOR THE COMPULSORY ENGLISH INTERVIEW: simply an e-mail with your personal details — "La modalita di iscrizione consiste nell'invio di un messaggio di posta elettronica all'indirizzo mail scienzepolitiche.orienta@unina.it con i propri dati" (a.y. 2026/2027 window 1-14 September 2026). In a.y. 2025/26 the same registration went to erminia.morone@unina.it. No fee and no form are mentioned. (2) FOR THE CURRICULAR/CREDIT CHECK: the Department's official form "Accesso Lauree Magistrali" (https://www.unina.it/documents/11958/24804618/SPOL_AccessoLM.doc), plus a complete transcript showing, for each exam, the grade, the number of CFU and the SSD (scientific-disciplinary sector), so the 48+12 CFU count against the L-36 ministerial table can be made. Related departmental forms: "Riconoscimento crediti CFU" (credit recognition), "Domanda di iscrizione a corsi singoli" (single course units, for making up missing credits), "Scelta curriculum" (choice of second-year curriculum). (3) ENGLISH PROFICIENCY: an official B2-or-higher certificate — the Regulations require "certified knowledge of English at least level B2" and the orientation portal says "Knowledge of the English language should be officially certified". No accepted-certificate list is published. (4) FOR NON-EU PRE-ENROLMENT ON UNIVERSITALY (uploaded as PDF), Master's track: Transcript of Records (ToR); Final degree certificate; Detailed course descriptions; Additional documents "e.g. language certificates, motivation letter, reference letters"; PRE-ACCEPTANCE LETTER FROM THE PROGRAMME COORDINATOR; and "DoV or CIMEA both Statement of comparability and verification". Plus, in the application form itself, personal details exactly as on the passport, and the Embassy/Consulate where the visa will be requested. The Italian tax code may be left blank at this stage but is required for enrolment. (5) QUALIFICATION-RECOGNITION DOCUMENTS (mandatory at enrolment): a Declaration of Value released by an Italian Embassy/Consulate — or, as an alternative, CIMEA Statement of Comparability AND Statement of Verification (jointly, https://cimea-diplome.it/). If the qualification comes from a European Higher Education Area / Bologna Process country: a DIPLOMA SUPPLEMENT accompanied by a CIMEA Statement of Verification. Holders of qualifications from Lisbon Recognition Convention signatory countries may use CIMEA's ARDI platform for a Statement of Correspondence plus a Statement of Verification. "At the enrolment stage, the above-mentioned documents are mandatory and must accompany the submitted/declared academic qualifications." (6) TO TAKE TO THE ITALIAN EMBASSY: the Universitaly pre-enrolment summary validated by the University; any language competence certificates; the visa-application documents including a health insurance policy; the foreign-qualification documents. Visa financial requirement: means of subsistence of 10,179.85 EUR per year, funds for repatriation, suitable accommodation and adequate medical insurance. (7) FOR ENROLMENT (MATRICULATION) AT THE STUDENT OFFICE — international students: copy of passport; application form; 1 passport photo; Italian tax code (codice fiscale); residence permit or proof of having applied for it; Declaration of Value or ENIC-NARIC/CIMEA certificate. "Important: always check the instructions on the degree programme's website." (8) FOR EU/ITALIAN ENROLMENT: the ordinary Federico II online procedure via www.segrepass.unina.it, followed by delivery of the printed plico, a passport photo, a photocopy of a valid identity document and — if the bachelor was taken elsewhere — a self-certification under D.P.R. 445/2000 of the degree and full exam list. Enquiries and paperwork: Segreteria Studenti Area didattica Scienze Politiche, Via Leopoldo Rodino 30/32, 80138 Napoli, segrescienzepol@unina.it. (9) ACCESSIBILITY REQUESTS (disability / invalidity / DSA) for the admission interview: send the departmental request form to dip.scienze-poltiche@unina.it and supporto.sinapsi@unina.it (deadline for a.y. 2026/2027 first session: 28 August 2026, 14:00). WHY UNCERTAIN: because the definitive international application document list is behind the external international-relations.net "Admission" page that this task's source restriction excluded, an additional programme-specific item (e.g. a motivation letter, CV or reference letters as a formal requirement rather than an "e.g.") may exist and is not captured here.
tuition_or_fees_link: OFFICIAL LINKS: https://www.unina.it/it/didattica/iscrizioni-e-tasse (Iscrizioni e tasse; English hub https://www.unina.it/en/didattica/iscrizioni-e-tasse) | binding 2026/27 document 'Guida all'iscrizione Anno accademico 2026-27': https://www.unina.it/documents/d/guest/guida_studente_rapida_26-27_10-7-2026 | official fee simulator: http://calcolatrice.unina.it/ | international-student summary: https://www.international.unina.it/education/admission-regulation/ | enrolment portal: https://www.segrepass.unina.it | Department's funding page pointing to https://www.unina.it/ateneo/study-in-naples ; regional grants and subsidised housing via ADISU Campania https://www.adisurcampania.it/ ; practical support (accommodation, codice fiscale, residence permit) via ISU Services. THE PROGRAMME'S OWN PAGES PUBLISH NO FIGURES — the Department page only says "The University of Naples Federico II offers a range of funding opportunities for international students, including tuition fee reductions and financial support." [uncertain] TWO DIFFERENT OFFICIAL PICTURES ARE PUBLISHED ON UNINA.IT AND MUST BE RECONCILED. (a) THE STANDARD ISEEU SYSTEM (Guida all'iscrizione 2026-27): the contribution depends on income (ISEE Universitario) and career (CFU earned). First-year students pay the "contributo agevolato" — fully EXEMPT with ISEEU up to 30,000 EUR; above that, a fixed component of 1,011.50 EUR plus a variable component, to a maximum of 2,384.00 EUR for those filing no ISEEU declaration. A 50% reduction applies to a first-year master's student who obtained the bachelor by October of the final year of the regular course with 110 cum laude. On top comes the regional right-to-study tax, banded at 130.00 EUR (ISEEU up to 25,500, and students from particularly poor countries under D.M. 176 of 24 February 2026), 151.00 EUR (ISEEU 25,500.01-51,000 AND students whose household resides abroad) and 173.00 EUR (ISEEU above 51,000 or no ISEEU declaration), plus 16.00 EUR stamp duty. (b) THE FLAT FOREIGN-CITIZEN RULES, which are what actually matter to an international applicant, set out among the exemptions in the same Guida: NON-EU CITIZENS ARE TOTALLY EXEMPT from the enrolment contribution — "stranieri (cittadinanza in Paesi extra UE): sono esonerati totalmente dal pagamento del contributo di iscrizione; devono versare solo la tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio ... e l'imposta di bollo" — so a non-EU student pays only the regional tax plus 16 EUR stamp. EU (non-Italian) CITIZENS pay only a fixed 200 EUR contribution where the calculated amount would be 200 EUR or more — "europei (cittadinanza in altri Paesi UE): sono tenuti solo al versamento di un contributo fisso pari a 200 EUR per l'iscrizione, se l'importo del contributo dovuto sia pari o superiore a 200 EUR." international.unina.it prints the same in round numbers: "Fees - Eropean students 200 EUR/year (tuition fees) + 140 EUR/year regional tax (compulsory) + 16.00 EUR legal stamp (compulsory) - Non-european students 140 EUR/year regional fee (compulsory) + 16.00 EUR legal stamp (compulsory)." NOTE THE MISMATCH: international.unina.it quotes a flat 140 EUR regional tax while the binding 2026/27 Guida gives 130/151/173 bands and assigns 151 EUR to students whose household resides abroad — the 140 figure appears carried over from an earlier year. REALISTIC ANNUAL COST for 2026/27: roughly 167 EUR for a non-EU student (151 + 16) and roughly 367 EUR for an EU non-Italian student (200 + 151 + 16). PAYMENT SCHEDULE: 1st instalment (60% + regional tax + stamp) by 2 November 2026; 2nd (20%) by 1 March 2027; 3rd (20%) by 30 April 2027; late-enrolment surcharges of 50 EUR (to 15 Jan 2027) and 110 EUR (from 16 Jan 2027); 100 EUR surcharge from 16 July 2027 for unpaid 2nd/3rd instalments. OTHER CHARGED SERVICES 2026/27: single-course (corsi singoli) enrolment 180 EUR; career reinstatement (ricognizione) 218 EUR including stamp; flat 202 EUR for students owing only the final exam and 380 EUR for those owing the final exam plus one other. Refunds are possible only where a statutory exemption applies; nothing is refunded on withdrawal from studies.
